samples.summary: The editor→preview palette wiring (`preview.setTheme(mode)`) has no test; both new editor tests pass if that line is deleted
samples.evidence: editor.ts:440-443 adds two behaviours on a theme switch: (a) repaint the preview, (b) push the new palette into NotePreview so mermaid re-renders in the new colours. The two new tests in editor.test.ts (`repaints the preview on a theme switch while it is visible`, `skips the theme repaint while the preview is hidden`) detect only (a) — they insert a `[data-role="repaint-marker"]` span and assert it is/isn't wiped, plus `querySelector('h1')`. Neither test stubs a mermaid loader or inspects the preview's mermaid theme, so removing `preview.setTheme(mode)` (leaving only `renderPreview()`) keeps both green while diagrams keep the stale palette — exactly the user-visible bug the comment says the change exists to prevent. preview.test.ts covers `NotePreview.setTheme` in isolation, but nothing covers the editor calling it.

samples.summary: No test asserts the `secure: SECURE_KEYS` list is passed to mermaid.initialize
samples.evidence: `SECURE_KEYS` is documented as one of the three security layers (it is what blocks `themeCSS`/`theme` overrides if a directive slips past `stripConfigDirectives`). The only assertions on the initialize config are `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark' })` (preview.test.ts:554) and `expect.objectContaining({ theme: 'dark', securityLevel: 'strict' })` (preview.test.ts:586-588). Dropping or truncating `secure: SECURE_KEYS` from the initialize call would not fail any test.
searchedFor: read all initialize assertions in preview.test.ts

samples.summary: sanitizeSvgMarkup is only tested for the malicious direction; nothing asserts legitimate mermaid SVG survives (internal `#id` refs, xlink:href, markers)
samples.evidence: preview.test.ts:361-390 feeds one hostile SVG and asserts things are removed. Real mermaid output relies on `url(#arrowhead)` in `style`/`marker-end` and on `xlink:href`/`href="#id"`; `scrubCss`'s `(?!#)` guard and `SAFE_URL_RE`'s `#` branch exist precisely to keep those, but no test exercises them. An over-aggressive scrub (e.g. dropping `url(#...)`) would silently break every real diagram's arrowheads with the whole suite still green. Also untested: the non-`script` members of DROPPED_TAGS (iframe, animate, set, …) and `xlink:href="javascript:..."`.
searchedFor: read sanitizeSvgMarkup and scrubCss in mermaid.ts
grep sanitizeSvgMarkup / xlink / url\(# in packages/notes/src
read the 'strips script and event handlers' test

samples.summary: stripConfigDirectives' selective front-matter rule is only tested in the stripping direction — no test that non-`config:` front matter (e.g. `title:`) is preserved
samples.evidence: The code deliberately drops front matter only when it contains a `config:` key (mermaid.ts:165). preview.test.ts:407-418 covers the `config:` case; there is no case with `---\ntitle: Foo\n---`, so a change that unconditionally sliced off front matter (breaking legitimate `title:`/`displayMode` front matter) would pass. `stripConfigDirectives` is also exported but has no direct unit test.
searchedFor: grep 'title:' / front matter fixtures in preview.test.ts

samples.summary: Fence-info matching (`lang.toLowerCase() === 'mermaid'`) untested for case variants and info strings with extra tokens
samples.evidence: preview.ts:76 lowercases the first info token. Every mermaid test in preview.test.ts uses the exact lowercase ```mermaid fence (grep of the test file shows only '```mermaid'), so neither ```Mermaid nor ```mermaid extra-token is covered, and the negative side (a ```mermaidjs fence must stay a code block) is untested too.

samples.summary: No test for a loader that rejects (as opposed to resolving null), i.e. the `.catch()` on the pass chain
samples.evidence: renderMermaidBlocks wraps the pass in `.catch()` so the chain survives and the promise never rejects; the failure mode tested is only `async () => null` (preview.test.ts:298-315). A throwing loader/engine-initialize would be swallowed by that catch, but nothing asserts the chain still works for the *next* pass afterwards, which is the stated reason the catch exists.
searchedFor: grep 'rejects'/'throw' in preview.test.ts mermaid describe block

samples.summary: apply()'s error-attribute clearing (a previously failing block later succeeding) is untested
samples.evidence: apply() removes `data-mermaid-error` and the `.note-mermaid-message` on a successful render. Tests cover fail-then-stay-failed and succeed-from-pending, but no case renders an error block and then a successful one for the same element/theme, so the clearing branch is never exercised.

finding.summary: The editor→preview palette wiring (`preview.setTheme(mode)`) has no test; both new editor tests pass if that line is deleted
finding.evidence: editor.ts:440-443 adds two behaviours on a theme switch: (a) repaint the preview, (b) push the new palette into NotePreview so mermaid re-renders in the new colours. The two new tests in editor.test.ts (`repaints the preview on a theme switch while it is visible`, `skips the theme repaint while the preview is hidden`) detect only (a) — they insert a `[data-role="repaint-marker"]` span and assert it is/isn't wiped, plus `querySelector('h1')`. Neither test stubs a mermaid loader or inspects the preview's mermaid theme, so removing `preview.setTheme(mode)` (leaving only `renderPreview()`) keeps both green while diagrams keep the stale palette — exactly the user-visible bug the comment says the change exists to prevent. preview.test.ts covers `NotePreview.setTheme` in isolation, but nothing covers the editor calling it.

verdict.reason: Verified the gap directly. editor.ts:432-444 does both a compartment reconfigure + preview.setTheme(mode) (line 442) + renderPreview() (line 443). preview.setTheme (preview.ts:193-195) only mutates a private mermaidTheme field whose sole observable effect flows through renderMermaidBlocks' theme option (preview.ts:208-211; mermaid.ts:260, 319-331), i.e. it is observable only with a stubbed mermaid engine. The two new editor tests (editor.test.ts:189-213, 215-243) assert only that a manually inserted [data-role="repaint-marker"] span is wiped/survives and that an h1 exists — both consequences of NotePreview.render()'s innerHTML replacement (preview.ts:198) alone, so deleting line 442 keeps them green. Searching wide for a counterexample: editor.ts:177 constructs NotePreview({ theme }) with no mermaidLoader seam, so no editor-level test can stub the engine; grep over packages for mermaidLoader/vi.mock(mermaid) hits only preview.test.ts and preview.ts; only editor.test.ts:4 and packages/frontend/src/app/notes/notes-undo-integration.test.ts:3 import initialize, and the latter contains no 'theme' occurrence at all; resetMermaidStateForTests/note-mermaid appear in tests only in preview.test.ts; preview.test.ts:574-589 exercises NotePreview.setTheme on a directly constructed preview, never via the editor; and there is no Playwright/e2e suite (glob for {e2e,tests,playwright}/** empty; backend *.e2e-spec.ts are HTTP/CLI only). No test anywhere fails if the editor stops forwarding the palette, so the user-visible stale-mermaid-colour behavior the change exists to fix is untested.
